summary: The Bahamas' Department of Immigration lists 155 countries, territories and islands (as of 8 October 2026) whose citizens need no visa for stays of up to three or eight months, as each agreement dictates; the Ministry of Foreign Affairs also lists Benin and Ghana as visa-free, but Bosnia and Herzegovina as needing a visa. Citizens of countries on the visa-required lists must obtain a visa before traveling. Every visitor presents a completed Bahamas Immigration Disembarkation/Embarkation Card at the border.

safety.text: The UK FCDO says there have been violent crimes and armed robberies, sometimes fatal, in residential and tourist areas of New Providence and Grand Bahama, and advises not going on foot outside the main tourist areas and beaches, avoiding unlit areas and travelling in groups after dusk. It warns never to go into water that has been baited to attract marine life.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for The Bahamas?
faq.answer: Most nationalities do not. The United States, Canada, the United Kingdom and the EU are among the 155 countries, territories and islands on the Department of Immigration's visa-waiver list (as of 8 October 2026), which allows stays of up to three or eight months, as each agreement dictates. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs also lists Benin and Ghana as visa-free, but Bosnia and Herzegovina as needing a visa. If your nationality is on the visa-required list, you must obtain a Bahamian visa before traveling.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a passport for The Bahamas?
faq.answer: Yes. The Department of Immigration requires every visitor to present a passport valid for at least six months, and states that passport cards are not accepted.

faq.question: Do I have to fill in a form before arriving?
faq.answer: Yes. Every visitor presents a completed Bahamas Immigration Disembarkation/Embarkation Card at the border, and passengers arriving by sea also complete the Inward Passenger and Crew Manifest. You must also declare cash or other valuables worth BSD 10,000 or more to customs.

faq.question: How long can I stay in The Bahamas?
faq.answer: The Department of Immigration says visa waivers allow stays of up to three or eight months, as each agreement dictates, without saying which applies to which country; Canada's travel advice says Canadians may stay up to 8 months without a tourist visa. The Department can extend a visitor's stay for a non-refundable $200 processing fee if you apply before the time granted expires.

faq.question: Can I work remotely from The Bahamas?
faq.answer: No official source we could read describes a remote-work visa or permit for The Bahamas. The Department of Immigration says visitors must not intend to engage in any gainful employment while in The Bahamas.
